transformationHistory: BodyParts3D OBJ (mm, normal situs) -> X reflected once, face winding reversed, 0.001 m/mm, offset [0.02357, 0.11538, -0.99441] m (Blender axes) = the v3 transform re-expressed in metres
liver: segments FJ2816/2818-2824/2409 pushed 2.45 mm along normals, 1.75 mm voxel remesh (union), Smooth 0.70 x 9, subdivision 1, collapse-decimated to 100000 triangles
gallbladder, stomach, duodenum, pancreas: subdivision 1 (pancreas decimated to the budget if needed)
gallbladder cut into fundus/body/infundibulum normal to its PCA long axis at 0.2/0.66

Layered Human centrelines: p = M.p + T with M = diag(-0.1, 0.1, 0.1) (mirror once, metres), T = [0.02593, 0.08565, 0.00486] m (fit, see anatomy.json portedCentrelineTransform); tubes swept along the source's Catmull-Rom spline with its radius profiles (x 0.1 m)

cystic artery (authored adjustments): points 1-2 lifted 1.5 mm out of the liver capsule; points 3-4 of the main course and 1-2 of the second branch landed on the free gallbladder serosa (+1 mm); origin on the RHA unchanged
authored: spleen ellipsoid, cystic plate patch, neck connector, wall model, landmarks, ports, regions
glTF export (Blender exporter, +Y up), no animation, no instruments
needsClinicalVerification: cystic artery course and branching (single artery from the right hepatic artery inside the hepatocystic triangle; distal landing authored; variants such as a double cystic artery or a low-lying origin not modelled)
ductal confluence position and the cystic-duct insertion (side, length, angle; low or medial insertion and parallel course not modelled)
tortuous gallbladder neck / Hartmann pouch not modelled specifically (authored straight neck connector)
right hepatic artery relation to the common hepatic duct (Layered Human course; caterpillar hump not modelled)
portal vein and left-sided branches ending at the liver surface (they stop within a few millimetres of the capsule)
laterality of every structure in situs inversus (mirrored reference anatomy, not the patient's imaging)
gallbladder size and orientation (BodyParts3D atlas body, ~6 cm long axis)
abdominal wall, costal margins, umbilicus, xiphoid and port positions (authored estimates)
cystic plate extent (authored patch under the lower third)
knownLimitations: the v3 liver processing (2.45 mm seam-closure push, remesh, smoothing) inflates the capsule by about 2 mm: 32 % of the gallbladder vertices lie inside the exported liver (the hepatic surface of the gallbladder is embedded in its bed, as in v3)

the Layered Human and BodyParts3D gallbladders differ by 18.8 deg in long-axis direction and 16 mm in length; one translation cannot match both the gallbladder and the porta (fit residuals in anatomy.json)
left portal vein, left hepatic duct and left hepatic artery end at the liver capsule rather than deep in the umbilical fissure (signed gaps in anatomy.json topology.enters)
the gallbladder parts are closed by flat caps at the cutting planes
